note: Pathway definitions. A variant's path is a list of nodes; node.mol is the molecule class carried on the segment LEAVING that node, node.label names the transporter/enzyme acting at the node. Anchors: sinusoid | gate:<id> | exo:sin | cytosol | canaliculus | mito | mito:matrix | mito:cristae | ser | rer | golgi | perox | lyso | ld | glyc | endo | nucleus. flux = relative weight fed/fasted (0-1). Crossings between the sinusoid and the cell membrane automatically route through an LSEC fenestra and the space of Disse. Anything uncertain is listed in ../UNCERTAINTIES.md.

pathways.name: Glucose handling
pathways.summary: Fed: GLUT2 uptake, glucokinase trapping, glycogen synthesis and glycolysis. Fasted: glycogenolysis and gluconeogenesis feed glucose-6-phosphatase in the ER and glucose leaves by GLUT2.
pathways.compartmentRoute: Sinusoid ⇄ space of Disse ⇄ GLUT2 ⇄ cytosol; fed: cytosol → glycogen / glycolysis → mitochondrion; fasted: glycogen or lactate → (mitochondrion) → cytosol → ER (G6PT, G6Pase) → cytosol → GLUT2 → sinusoid
pathways.direction: Net influx when portal glucose is high (fed, insulin); net efflux when fasted (glucagon).
pathways.clinical: Glycogen storage disease type Ia (G6PC1 deficiency): fasting hypoglycaemia with hepatomegaly, lactic acidosis, hyperlipidaemia. Insulin resistance in MASLD leaves gluconeogenesis unsuppressed in the fed state, contributing to hyperglycaemia.

path.label: Glucose leaves the ER (exit route uncertain)
MCT (lactate uptake; Cori cycle) — LDH → pyruvate

pathways.name: Fatty acid handling
pathways.summary: Free fatty acids enter via CD36/FATPs, are activated to acyl-CoA and either oxidised in mitochondria (acetyl-CoA → TCA/OXPHOS → ATP, or ketogenesis) or esterified to triglyceride for VLDL secretion or storage in lipid droplets.
pathways.compartmentRoute: Sinusoid → space of Disse → CD36/FATP → cytosol (FABP1, ACSL1) → (a) mitochondrion: CPT1A → matrix β-oxidation → acetyl-CoA → TCA/OXPHOS or ketogenesis; (b) SER/RER: triglyceride → VLDL assembly (MTTP, ApoB100) → Golgi → exocytosis → space of Disse → sinusoid; (c) SER → lipid droplet
pathways.direction: Uptake from blood, oxidation and ketone export dominate fasted; esterification and VLDL secretion dominate fed. Malonyl-CoA (insulin-driven) inhibits CPT1A in the fed state.
pathways.clinical: Steatosis (MASLD): ≥5% of hepatocytes contain fat when uptake and de novo lipogenesis exceed oxidation and VLDL export. Impaired mitochondrial β-oxidation (valproate, acute fatty liver of pregnancy, Reye) gives microvesicular steatosis. Abetalipoproteinaemia (MTTP loss) traps triglyceride because VLDL cannot be assembled.

path.label: TCA cycle → respiratory chain → ATP synthase
GPAT → AGPAT → LPIN → DGAT: triglyceride synthesis in ER
MTTP + ApoB100: VLDL particle assembly in ER lumen
Exocytosis into the space of Disse
DGAT1/2: triglyceride lens forms between ER leaflets

pathways.name: Protein synthesis & secretion
pathways.summary: Amino acids are taken up, assembled on ribosomes of the rough ER into secretory proteins (albumin, clotting factors, fibrinogen), processed in the Golgi and secreted at the sinusoidal face into the space of Disse.
pathways.compartmentRoute: Sinusoid → space of Disse → amino-acid carrier → cytosol → RER (ribosome, translocon, lumen) → ER exit sites (COPII) → Golgi cis → trans → secretory vesicle → exocytosis at sinusoidal face → space of Disse → LSEC fenestra → sinusoid
pathways.direction: Amino acids in; secretory proteins out at the sinusoidal (basolateral) pole. Bile proteins/lipids leave at the canalicular pole by separate routes.
pathways.clinical: Synthetic dysfunction in liver failure: low albumin, prolonged INR (factors II, V, VII, IX, X). α1-antitrypsin deficiency (PiZZ): misfolded Z-AAT polymers accumulate in the RER (PAS-positive diastase-resistant globules) with liver injury and low circulating AAT.

path.label: Ribosome + Sec61: nascent chain enters RER lumen; folding, N-glycosylation
COPII vesicles → Golgi: glycan maturation, sorting

pathways.name: Ammonia → urea
pathways.summary: Ammonia (portal, from gut bacteria and amino-acid catabolism) is converted to urea by the urea cycle, which spans the mitochondrial matrix (CPS1, OTC) and cytosol (ASS1, ASL, ARG1). Urea leaves to blood.
pathways.compartmentRoute: Sinusoid → space of Disse → cytosol → mitochondrial matrix (CPS1, OTC: carbamoyl phosphate → citrulline) → ORNT1 → cytosol (ASS1, ASL, ARG1: arginine → urea + ornithine) → urea to sinusoid; ornithine returns to the matrix via ORNT1
pathways.direction: Nitrogen enters from blood and leaves as urea; ornithine cycles between cytosol and matrix.
pathways.clinical: Hyperammonaemia in cirrhosis (reduced hepatocyte mass and portosystemic shunting) drives hepatic encephalopathy; urea-cycle enzyme defects (OTC deficiency, X-linked) present with hyperammonaemia. The perivenous glutamine synthetase pool is the high-affinity backup scavenger.

path.label: CPS1 (NH4+ + HCO3- + 2 ATP → carbamoyl-P) → OTC (+ ornithine) → citrulline

pathways.name: Bilirubin
pathways.summary: Albumin-bound unconjugated bilirubin is taken up (OATP1B1/1B3), conjugated with glucuronic acid by UGT1A1 in the smooth ER, and the water-soluble conjugates are pumped into the canaliculus by MRP2. A minor MRP3 route returns conjugates to blood.
pathways.compartmentRoute: Sinusoid → space of Disse → OATP1B1/1B3 → cytosol → SER (UGT1A1) → cytosol → MRP2 at the canalicular membrane → bile canaliculus
pathways.direction: Sinusoid → canaliculus (net). MRP3 efflux back to sinusoid is minor and increases in cholestasis.
pathways.clinical: Unconjugated hyperbilirubinaemia: Gilbert syndrome (reduced UGT1A1 expression), Crigler–Najjar (severe/absent UGT1A1). Conjugated hyperbilirubinaemia from failed canalicular export: Dubin–Johnson (MRP2/ABCC2 loss) and cholestasis generally. Urine bilirubin appears only when conjugated.

pathways.name: Bile acids
pathways.summary: Conjugated bile acids returning from the gut (enterohepatic circulation) are taken up by NTCP. New bile acids are made from cholesterol (CYP7A1 in the ER), finished and conjugated in peroxisomes/cytosol. BSEP pumps them into the canaliculus.
pathways.compartmentRoute: Uptake: sinusoid → space of Disse → NTCP → cytosol → BSEP → canaliculus. Synthesis: cholesterol (ER) → CYP7A1 → peroxisome (side-chain shortening, conjugation) → cytosol → BSEP → canaliculus
pathways.direction: Sinusoid → canaliculus. NTCP is Na+-coupled inward; BSEP is ATP-dependent outward, the rate-limiting step for bile-salt-dependent bile flow.
pathways.clinical: Cholestasis: BSEP dysfunction (PFIC2, drug-induced BSEP inhibition, benign recurrent intrahepatic cholestasis), intrahepatic cholestasis of pregnancy. NTCP is the hepatocyte entry receptor for hepatitis B/D viruses. Bile-acid retention drives pruritus and hepatocyte injury.

path.label: CYP7A1 (rate-limiting) → CYP8B1 / CYP27A1 → cholic / chenodeoxycholic acid
ACOX2 side-chain shortening; BAAT conjugation (glycine / taurine)

pathways.name: Xenobiotic metabolism
pathways.summary: Drugs and toxins enter, are oxidised by smooth-ER CYP450 enzymes (phase I), conjugated (phase II: UGT, SULT, GST) and exported into bile (MRP2, P-gp, BCRP) or back to blood (MRP3/4) for renal excretion.
pathways.compartmentRoute: Sinusoid → space of Disse → uptake carrier or diffusion → SER (CYP450) → SER lumen / cytosol (conjugation) → canalicular MRP2/P-gp/BCRP → bile, or sinusoidal MRP3/4 → blood
pathways.direction: Inward at the sinusoidal pole; outward at either pole depending on the size and polarity of the conjugate (larger amphipathic conjugates favour bile).
pathways.clinical: Drug-induced liver injury: paracetamol overdose (CYP2E1/3A4 → NAPQI, glutathione depletion), idiosyncratic DILI, cholestatic injury from BSEP/MRP2 inhibition. CYP induction (rifampicin, phenobarbital, alcohol) and inhibition (macrolides, azoles) underlie drug interactions.

variants.name: Phase I → Phase II → biliary export

path.label: Phase II: UGT / SULT / GST conjugation
MRP3 / MRP4: efflux to blood (renal excretion)

pathways.name: Cholesterol & lipoprotein remnants
pathways.summary: Chylomicron remnants and LDL are taken up by receptor-mediated endocytosis, hydrolysed in lysosomes (LAL), and free cholesterol is exported by NPC1/NPC2 to the ER pool, from which it is secreted into bile (ABCG5/G8), esterified for storage, converted to bile acids or packaged into VLDL.
pathways.compartmentRoute: Sinusoid → space of Disse → LDLR/LRP1/HSPG → clathrin-coated vesicle → endosome → lysosome (LAL) → NPC2/NPC1 → ER cholesterol pool → (a) ABCG5/G8 → canaliculus, (b) cholesteryl ester in lipid droplet, (c) CYP7A1 → bile acids, (d) VLDL
pathways.direction: Remnants and LDL in from blood; free cholesterol out to bile (ABCG5/G8) or stored/reused.
pathways.clinical: Lysosomal acid lipase deficiency (Wolman disease / CESD): hepatomegaly, microvesicular steatosis and cholesteryl-ester accumulation. LDLR defects cause familial hypercholesterolaemia. ABCG5/G8 loss-of-function causes sitosterolaemia; common ABCG8 variants raise gallstone risk.

variants.name: Remnant / LDL uptake → lysosome → ER pool

path.label: Lysosomal acid lipase (LIPA); NPC2 → NPC1 export free cholesterol
ER cholesterol pool (SREBP2 sensing; ACAT2 esterification)
Cholesteryl ester in lipid droplet core
